description: Fundamentals of gardening, plant care, soil science, and growing food

soil_types.clay: Dense, holds moisture well, drains poorly, nutrient-rich
soil_types.sandy: Drains well, warms quickly, loses nutrients fast
soil_types.loam: Ideal mix of sand, silt, clay; well-draining and fertile

soil_science.ph_scale: 6.0–7.0 ideal for most vegetables; acidic soil released by sulfur, raised by lime

amendments.compost: Decomposed organic matter; improves all soil types

npk.nitrogen_N: Leaf and stem growth; deficiency causes yellowing

watering.general_rule: Water deeply and infrequently to encourage deep root growth
watering.finger_test: Insert finger 2cm into soil; water if dry
watering.morning_best: Morning watering reduces disease risk from overnight moisture
watering.drip_irrigation: Most efficient; delivers water directly to roots

planting_basics.hardiness_zones: USDA map dividing regions by average minimum winter temperature
planting_basics.frost_dates: Last spring frost and first fall frost determine growing season
planting_basics.seed_starting: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost; use seed-starting mix
planting_basics.transplanting: Harden off seedlings for 7–10 days before outdoor planting
planting_basics.spacing: Follow package instructions; overcrowding causes disease and competition

cool_season.planting: Early spring or fall; tolerate light frost

warm_season.planting: After last frost; need warm soil (16°C+)

composting.green_materials: Nitrogen-rich; fresh grass, vegetable scraps, coffee grounds
composting.process: Layer materials; keep moist; turn every 1–2 weeks; ready in 2–6 months

pest_and_disease_management.ipm: Integrated Pest Management; use least toxic methods first
